text:
lisa: Kicking off a short thread on GCP KMS layouts for Private installs. We need a clear ops + security playbook: customer-key-in-customer-project vs keys-in-host-project with impersonation. pros/cons and concrete IAM + audit steps?

sam: TL;DR: customer-project keys => best for compliance + clear audit ownership. host-project keys => simpler for infra (single rotation, single sink). Both valid; pick based on customer requirement.

maria: Compliance notes: If customer requires their own key control (regulatory requirement), put keys in their project and export audit logs there. Otherwise host-project + strong impersonation + immutable audit export to customer works.

neil: Operational note: We usually create a per-customer service account in the customer project (cust-sa@cust-project) and give it roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on cryptoKeys. Then grant a minimal host infra principal iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on that SA for short-lived impersonation. Avoid long-lived cross-project keys.

elllen: small typo in my head ^^ ellen: Example IAM bindings we recommend: at cryptoKey level grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the cust-service-account. For a host-initiated rewrap job, grant roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to infra@redwood-host.iam.gserviceaccount.com on the cust-sa.

ops-bot: reminder: prefer least-privilege and scoped bindings (cryptoKey rather than keyRing) when possible.

sam: Concrete gcloud example we use in playbooks:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/CUST-P/locations/global/keyRings/CUST-R/cryptoKeys/CUST-K \\  --member=serviceAccount:cust-sa@CUST-P.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding CUST-P --member=serviceAccount:infra@redwood-host.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

maria: Audit config: enable ADMIN_READ + DATA_ACCESS for KMS in customer project. DATA_ACCESS is off by default, but for Private we enable it and export to a locked sink (pubsub/bigquery) in the customer's project so they own retention. If using host keys, replicate logs to customer's sink and mark them as immutable if required.

neil: Envelope encryption pattern: apps generate a random DEK per object, wrap DEK with KMS (Encrypt) -> store wrapped DEK alongside ciphertext. At read, Unwrap (Decrypt) to get DEK, decrypt object, zero DEK memory. Avoid storing plaintext DEKs.

lisa: For rotation, do we prefer server-side rewrap or offline rewrap jobs? KMS doesn't have native server-side rewrap API so we'll need an orchestrated rewrap. Thoughts on safe implementation?

sam: Phased rewrap is safest: create new key version, mark it primary for new wraps, then run a controlled rewrap job to migrate wrapped DEKs. Keep both keys valid during migration to avoid downtime.

maria: Security reminders for rewrap job: run in ephemeral, patched containers; limit SA to only Decrypt old key + Encrypt new key; log all calls; rotate the job's SA after use. Consider running rewrap inside customer's VPC for compliance.

elllen: Implementation options:
- Batch rewrap workers (K8s jobs) that pull a page of records, call KMS decrypt -> encrypt, update record; workers auto-scale with rate limit.
- Single-use Cloud Run/Cloud Function per-customer for small datasets.
- If scale is huge, implement versioned wrapped keys in DB so reads can still use older wrapped DEK until that object is migrated.

neil: Important: never persist plaintext DEKs to logs or storage. Use in-memory only and explicit zeroing if language supports it.

maria: Emergency rotation playbook (high-level):
1) Create new cryptoKeyVersion and promote (primary).
2) Pause write services from using old primary (or have them start wrapping with new primary).
3) Launch rewrap job with strict RBAC.
4) Monitor decrypt counts and anomalies (use logs-based metrics + alerts).
5) After migration, schedule old key versions for destruction per retention policy.
6) Rotate any compromised SA credentials and revoke tokens.

lisa: Monitoring and alerting suggestions?

sam: Create logs-based metric on KMS Decrypt count per SA/region, alert on spikes or decrypts from unfamiliar principals. Also instrument rewrap progress dashboards (items processed, failures).

maria: Add periodic audit run that lists key bindings and checks for iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator grants scoped to expected infra SAs only. Flag unexpected principals.

elllen: Terraform snippet for cryptoKey binding to a SA (for docs repo):
```
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "wrap_sa" {
  crypto_key_id = "projects/${var.project}/locations/global/keyRings/${var.ring}/cryptoKeys/${var.key}"
  role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  members       = ["serviceAccount:${var.sa_email}"]
}
```

neil: Gotcha: if host-project keys are used and customer wants proof-of-use, we must set up log exports and provide immutable snapshots or a signed ledger. Plan this early in onboarding.

maria: Also consider key naming & keyRing naming conventions: include tenant-id, environment, and an immutable UID (avoid predictable names if you want secrecy).

lisa: Next steps: I'll draft a short playbook with both patterns (customer-hosted & host-hosted) that includes: IAM bindings, audit export steps, rewrap job template, and emergency rotation checklist. Can folks review tomorrow?

elllen: I can take infra TF and rewrap job templates.

maria: I'll review IAM, logging, and the emergency steps.

neil: I'll vet the rewrap performance implications and worker sizing.

sam: Ping me for final infra permissions and onboarding docs.

ops-bot: action created: kb/infra/private-kms-playbook - draft assigned to lisa, review channel eng-security. Due: 72h.

lisa: Thanks all, posting draft when ready. :thumbsup:
